options: The model's permanent long-term memory of you
The time of day the model works best
Everything the model can currently see and use — messages, shown files, tool results — with a size limit
The app window where you type

explain.right: The context window is the limited set of text the model can see right now; anything outside it effectively doesn't exist for it.
explain.wrong: It isn't a UI element or permanent memory; the model has no persistent memory of you across the window being cleared.

items.q: You want the AI to fix a bug in your file. Which prompt will most reliably work?
options: Paste the file + the exact error + what it should do instead
"You should already know what I mean."

explain.right: Specific goal + the actual material (file + error) gives the model what it needs to predict a correct fix.
explain.wrong: Vague requests with no context force the model to guess, which invites wrong or generic answers.

items.q: Why can a very long chat start giving worse answers?
options: Early details fall out of the context window as it fills, so the model loses the thread
Long chats are always better, this never happens

explain.right: As the window fills, older content is summarized or dropped, so the model can lose earlier details and drift.
explain.wrong: Models don't tire, and more history is not automatically better — relevance beats volume.

items.q: Rewrite this weak prompt to be good: 'make the login nicer'. What would you add?
rubric: Provides the relevant material (the file/component, a screenshot or example)

explain.right: Strong answers add concrete specifics and hand over the actual file/example plus the intended result.
explain.wrong: Just saying 'add please' or more adjectives isn't enough — specificity and material are the point.
